title: Rebase instead of merge
summary: Exercise 5: replay your commit on top of the new develop.

say.never: You made your branch a while ago, and since then `develop` moved ahead without you: someone added commit **X**. Your branch is now a little *behind*, and the history has a fork in it.
say.bit: You branched a while ago, and develop moved on without you.

board.code:
develop        o---o---X        (X: a new commit)
issue-15            \--R      (your RAINBOW commit)

marks.label: your commit, based on old develop

say.never: **Rebasing** picks up your commits and puts them back down on top of `develop`'s newest commit, as if you had only just started. Instead of a fork there's one straight line. The new copy of your commit is marked `R'`.
say.bit: Rebasing **replays** your commits on top of develop's newest commit, as if you'd started there. No merge commit, a straight line.

marks.label: the same change, replayed on X

say.never: Stand on **your** branch, then tell git to rebase it onto `develop`. The last command draws the history as a picture, so you can see the straight line.
say.bit: Stand on **your** branch and rebase it onto develop.

board.code:
git checkout issue-15-led-colors
git rebase develop
git log --oneline --graph --all

say.never: Open the **terminal**: the typing area at the bottom of the screen where you give the computer instructions. Hold **Ctrl** and tap the backtick key, the one above **Tab**. Most of these exercises are easier there.
say.bit: These exercises are easiest in the terminal.

hint.never: press Ctrl and the backtick key (above Tab).

say.never: Type `cd 05-rebase` and press **Enter**. Then run the three commands on the board, one at a time. When you're done, the picture should be one straight line.
say.bit: `cd 05-rebase`, then run them. The graph should be one straight line.

say.never: Rebase keeps the history tidy, but it **rewrites** your commits, giving them new identities. So only rebase a branch that nobody else has copied yet. If you're not sure, just merge. Merging is always safe.
say.bit: Rebase keeps history straight, but it **rewrites** your commits. Only rebase branches nobody else has pulled yet. When in doubt, merge.
